'''''Zygophyllum fabago''''' is a species of plant known by the common name '''Syrian bean-caper'''. It is considered a [[Noxious weeds|noxious weed]] of economic importance in much of the western United States. It is native to Asia, East Europe (Russia and Ukraine), and Southeast Europe (Romania).<ref name=GRIN/>

==Growth==
The Syrian bean-caper grows long, thin stems with few oval-shaped, fleshy, waxy green leaflets each 2 to 3 centimeters in length. The flowers are small, compact bunches of five petals each with prominent stamens. The flowers have a taste and scent similar to [[caper]]. It grows in masses of individual plants, forming colonies, especially in dry, gravelly, saline, or disturbed areas where other plant life is rare.

==Characteristics==
The plant has invasive potential due to its long [[taproot]] which, even if fragmented, can produce a new plant, as well as the hardy wax coating on its leaves that tends to protect it from [[herbicide]]s.

==Chemical constituents==
It contains about 0.002% [[harmine]] (entire plant).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.erowid.org/library/books_online/ayahuasca_apa/aya_sec2_zygophyllaceae.shtml |title=Erowid Online Books : "Ayahuasca: alkaloids, plants, and analogs" by Keeper of the Trout |publisher=www.erowid.org |access-date=2008-04-30}}</ref>
